readings: For y=101,110,111, Y0 and z are don't-cares; synthesis may assign arbitrary values (e.g., Y=000, z=0), so outputs can be 0 or 1 depending on implementation.

For y=101,110,111, the design must define explicit next-state and output behavior (e.g., self-loop with Y=y,z=0 or transition to 000 with z=0), but the table omits these rows, so two engineers can choose different fixed outputs.
Combinational outputs: Y0 and z are functions of current x and y; clk is ignored, so outputs change in the same cycle as inputs.
Sequential outputs: Y0 and z are registered on clk (e.g., rising edge), so they update one cycle later and hold between clock edges.
No reset is provided, so if any register exists its power-up value is unspecified and outputs may be unknown until a known transition occurs.
The module is purely combinational, so reset is irrelevant and outputs are always determined by x and y.
